audio_script_it:
Buongiorno, benvenuti al Morning Briefing di Price Alert.

Il Nikkei ha chiuso in calo dell'1.02%, Shanghai in rialzo dello 0.71%. Questo suggerisce un'apertura debole per i mercati europei.

Nella seduta di nella seduta precedente, l'S&P 500 ha chiuso in calo dello 0.49%, il VIX è salito dello 0.67% a 17.95 Il Dollar Index è in rialzo dello 0.1% a 98.72 L'oro è sceso dello 0.26% a $4579.4 l'oncia. Il petrolio è in calo del 3.64% a $107.21 Il rendimento del decennale americano è salito dello 0.42% al 4.35%.

La Banca del Giappone ha mantenuto i tassi invariati e ha alzato le previsioni d'inflazione a causa dei timori sulla guerra in Iran. Questo ha avuto un impatto sui mercati.

Oggi in agenda il PIL degli Stati Uniti. Nessun'altra notizia macroeconomica rilevante in uscita oggi.

Passiamo ora al comparto degli asset digitali. Bitcoin si mantiene sopra i settantasettemila dollari con una variazione del 0,25%. Gli ETF hanno registrato deflussi significativi per 89,7 milioni di dollari. Questo movimento potrebbe essere influenzato dalle recenti dichiarazioni di Paul Tudor Jones, che considera Bitcoin come la migliore copertura contro l'inflazione.

Per quanto riguarda le altcoin, Ethereum guadagna l'1,65% arrivando a duemilatrecento dollari, mentre Solana cresce dello 0,74% a ottantaquattro dollari e quarantanove centesimi. BNB registra una crescita modesta dello 0,12% a seicentoventicinque dollari e tredici centesimi.

Il Fear & Greed Index è a 26, in territorio di Fear, suggerisce cautela sugli investitori.

Grazie per aver ascoltato il nostro podcast finanziario. Per domani, tenete d'occhio l'evoluzione dei mercati europei e americani, e monitorate gli sviluppi sulle principali borse. Un saluto da Price Alert, arrivederci alla prossima puntata. Grazie per l'attenzione e a domani.
audio_script_en: Good morning, welcome to the Price Alert Morning Briefing. The Nikkei closed down 1.02%, while Shanghai rose 0.71%. This suggests a weak opening for European markets. In the previous session, the S&P 500 closed down 0.49%, and the VIX rose 0.67% to 17.95 The Dollar Index is up 0.1% to 98.72 Gold fell 0.26% to $4,579.4 per ounce. Oil is down 3.64% to $107.21 The US 10-year yield rose 0.42% to 4.35%. The Bank of Japan kept interest rates unchanged and raised its inflation forecasts due to concerns over the war in Iran, which had an impact on markets. Today's agenda features the US GDP release. There are no other significant macroeconomic news releases scheduled for today. Let's pivot to the cryptocurrency markets... Bitcoin remains above $77,000 with a 0.25% change. ETFs saw significant outflows of $89.7 million. This movement may be influenced by recent statements from Paul Tudor Jones, who considers Bitcoin the best hedge against inflation. Regarding altcoins, Ethereum gains 1.65% to $2,300, while Solana grows 0.74% to $84.49 BNB registers a modest 0.12% growth to $625.13 The Fear & Greed Index is at 26, in Fear territory, suggesting caution for investors. Thanks for listening to our financial podcast. For tomorrow, keep an eye on the evolution of European and American markets, and monitor developments on major stock exchanges. A greeting from Price Alert, see you in the next episode. Thanks for your attention, and goodbye.

articles.title: Book launch: World War Trade: Conflict, Containment, and the Emergent World Trading Order
articles.snippet: Globalization is not dying. It is being rebuilt. When the United States and China weaponized trade in 2025, many feared the collapse of the global economy. Markets plunged, supply chains fractured, and policymakers spoke openly of economic warfare. But the collapse never came. In his new book, World War Trade, published by the Centre for Economic Policy Research, Richard Baldwin argues that the real story is not the conflict between superpowers but how the rest of the world responded. Through quiet restraint, strategic adaptation, and a wave of new trade agreements, countries representing the…

articles.title: The Strange Rise and Fall of Russia’s Crowd Sourced Defense Industry
articles.snippet: In the early days of the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, much that could go wrong did for the Russian military. Three or four days later, Katya’s husband (who served with Donetsk militia) disappeared from communications. We searched for him every day through the commandant’s office to make sure everything was alright. articles.title: UK Borrowing Costs Hit Highest Since 2008 as Oil Tops $111
articles.snippet: The government’s borrowing costs have risen to their joint highest level since the 2008 financial crisis, after a sharp jump in the oil price prompted a sell-off in UK debt because of concerns over inflation. The yield on the 10-year gilt – the main benchmark for any government’s long-term ability to borrow – climbed back above five per cent for only the third time since the Iran war broke out on Tuesday, laying bare the extent to which Britain is almost uniquely exposed to the ongoing energy shock. articles.title: Higher Oil Prices Lift Sinopec Profit 28% in First Quarter
articles.snippet: China’s top refiner posted a strong first quarter as higher crude prices lifted inventory values and stable domestic fuel sales helped to offset pressure from disrupted Middle East supply. China Petroleum & Chemical Corporation (Sinopec) reported first-quarter net income of 17 billion yuan ($2.49 billion), up 28% from a year earlier, according to a Shanghai exchange filing. The results land as major oil companies begin showing how the Iran-driven supply shock is feeding through earnings. Throughput at Sinopec slipped 0.2% year over year…
